findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Handle non-default tracker layouts in the show_ticket(repo_root=...) construction (or document the default-name assumption): tracker_dir honors REBAR_TRACKER_DIR and absolute/renamed tracker.dir, so Path(tracker_git_root).parent is not guaranteed to round-trip.
evidence: Plan: "config.tracker_dir(repo_root), which appends .tickets-tracker to repo_root — so repo_root must be the tracker dir's PARENT"
config.py:145-159: env override returns verbatim; configured absolute tracker.dir returned verbatim; only the ConfigError/default path appends '.tickets-tracker'
findings.finding: The plan states show_ticket resolves via config.tracker_dir(repo_root) 'which appends .tickets-tracker to repo_root', but config.tracker_dir (config.py:138) applies full precedence — REBAR_TRACKER_DIR wins verbatim and an absolute/renamed configured tracker.dir relocates the store — so constructing repo_root as Path(tracker_git_root).parent only yields the right tracker under the default name.
findings.location: Context § (show_ticket paragraph) and Approach § 'Ticket-level event source' (repo_root=str(Path(tracker_git_root).parent))
scenarios: A corpus store whose tracker was relocated via REBAR_TRACKER_DIR or an absolute tracker.dir — show_ticket(repo_root=<parent>) then resolves to the wrong (or default) tracker, silently dropping caused_by/close_class labels for that store

evidence: Plan: "reopen_count/force_close/completion_verifier_fail_count reuse mine_outcome_corpus.py's pure functions of that name"
mine_outcome_corpus.py:200/209/216 define these as module-level functions under docs/experiments/plan-review-gate/harnesses/
The new artifact is src/rebar/llm/evals/plan_replay/labels.py — a production src/ module importing from a docs/ experiment harness
findings.finding: The miner pure functions reopen_count/force_close/completion_verifier_fail_count the plan reuses live in docs/experiments/plan-review-gate/harnesses/mine_outcome_corpus.py (a docs/ harness outside the new module's artifact dir), so reusing them from src/rebar/llm/evals/plan_replay/labels.py implies a src->docs import direction that the plan neither enumerates nor resolves (import vs copy vs lift-to-shared-module).
scenarios: labels.py `from docs.experiments... import reopen_count` — docs/ is typically not an importable package root
The harness is later moved/refactored and silently breaks the production module
findings.suggested_fix: Lift the three pure functions (plus the STATUS/COMMENT/COMPLETION_VERDICT git-walk they need) into a small shared helper under src/rebar/llm/evals/plan_replay/ and have both the harness and labels.py import from there.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State explicitly whether labels.py labels the verified-only corpus cache (loaded from <content_hash>.jsonl) or its own independent blob re-enumeration, and make the labeled review/ticket set provably identical to the population content_hash is computed over.
evidence: corpus.build_corpus returns `manifest` only (no rows); the plan's Context also lists only manifest keys
_write_cache: `if not row["verified"]: continue` — the <content_hash>.jsonl contains verified rows ONLY
Plan: labels 'reuse corpus._enumerate_event_blobs + corpus._batch_cat to re-read recovered REVIEW_RESULT blobs' — an INDEPENDENT re-enumeration, not a consumption of corpus rows
AC: 'Every review and finding in the corpus carries the labels' — 'in the corpus' is ambiguous between the verified-only cache and labels.py's own recovered set
findings.finding: The plan does not reconcile the review/ticket set that labels.py labels with the corpus that content_hash actually pins: build_corpus returns only the manifest and _write_cache persists ONLY verified rows, while labels.py re-enumerates REVIEW_RESULT blobs and re-walks per-store events independently — so 'every review and finding in the corpus carries labels' is under-specified as to whether the labeled set is the verified-only cache, all recovered sidecars, or labels.py's own re-enumeration.
findings.location: Approach → 'Finding-level source' and 'Ticket-level event source'; corpus.py build_corpus/_write_cache
scenarios: A recovered but UNVERIFIED (fingerprint-mismatch) review: is it labeled? It is absent from the cache the content_hash keys, yet present in labels.py's independent blob re-read.
A norm_id pair where one review verified and the other did not — the consecutive-review join may include a review the corpus deliberately excluded.
findings.suggested_fix: Have labels.py load the frozen <content_hash>.jsonl verified rows as the definitive population (or have corpus expose the verified rows alongside the manifest), and drive both the finding-level join and the per-ticket show_ticket/git-walk over exactly that id/review set — so the labeled set is identical to what content_hash pins.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Note in the labels report whether the raw micro-averaged Pass-2 agreement is intended purely as a descriptive noise floor, and briefly state why a chance-corrected coefficient (kappa / Krippendorff's alpha) is out of scope here (or record it as deferred).
evidence: Plan: 'agreement is micro-averaged: (# flattened-key-comparisons where old value == new value) / (total flattened-key-comparisons)'

Retrieved prior art: arXiv 'Counting on Consensus: Selecting the Right Inter-annotator Agreement...' — 'relying on raw agreement alone can overestimate reliability, motivating the use of chance-corrected and task-appropriate statistics'
Retrieved prior art: ACM dl.acm.org/doi/fullHtml/10.1145/3485447.3512242 — Krippendorff's alpha as the standard agreement coefficient
The plan frames this as a descriptive noise floor and publishes the pooled comparison count, so raw agreement is defensible for that purpose — this is a consideration, not a blocking gap
findings.finding: The noise-floor 'per-question Pass-2 agreement' is published as a raw micro-averaged agreement fraction with no consideration of established chance-corrected inter-rater agreement coefficients (Cohen's/Fleiss' kappa, Krippendorff's alpha), which the IAA literature treats as the standard when characterizing rater/label reliability.
findings.location: Approach → 'Noise floor' bullet, item (c) per-question Pass-2 agreement; Acceptance Criteria line 2
scenarios: A later ticket or reader interprets the published agreement fraction as a reliability figure and compares it against kappa-based numbers from other calibration work, without the chance-correction baseline that makes such comparison meaningful
findings.suggested_fix: Add one sentence to the 'Noise floor' bullet clarifying the agreement figure is a descriptive raw-agreement floor (not a chance-corrected reliability statistic), and flag chance-corrected IAA as an explicit non-goal for a later ticket.

Scope lists only 'src/rebar/llm/evals/plan_replay/labels.py (new)', the report, and the test — corpus.py is not listed
'labels.py's own per-store git-walk' suggests a local reimplementation, but 'extending corpus._enumerate_event_blobs's content-type filter' suggests editing corpus.py — the two readings conflict
findings.finding: The Approach says the git-walk is done by 'extending corpus._enumerate_event_blobs's content-type filter to also recover STATUS/COMMENT/COMPLETION_VERDICT blobs', but Scope lists only labels.py, the report, and the test — not corpus.py. It is unclear whether corpus.py (a CLOSED ticket's module) is being edited, or whether labels.py reimplements the walk locally. An executor cannot tell whether to modify a private function in an out-of-scope module.
findings.location: Approach — 'Ticket-level event source (multi-store, corrected units)' bullet; Scope section
scenarios: Executor edits corpus.py's private filter, silently changing behavior for its existing (closed) consumers
Executor reimplements the walk in labels.py, duplicating logic and drifting from corpus.py
findings.suggested_fix: Add labels.py's own `_enumerate_event_blobs`-style walk that accepts the desired content-type set as a parameter, leaving corpus.py untouched; or explicitly add corpus.py to Scope with the filter made parameterizable.
